Implementation-relevant•Peer-reviewed real-world clinical and analytical performance study•September 28, 2026

Routine LUMIPULSE p-tau217 stayed stable across 18 months

In 744 cognitively impaired Mayo Clinic patients, a laboratory-developed LUMIPULSE plasma p-tau217 workflow classified amyloid pathology with 93% accuracy among definite results; 23% were intermediate, while quality-control imprecision was 5%–8% and lot-to-lot bias remained within 11% over 18 months.

Key quantitative results: Of 744 patients, 500 (67%) were amyloid-positive. Plasma p-tau217 results were positive in 421 (57%), intermediate in 169 (23%) and negative in 154 (21%). Excluding intermediate results, sensitivity was 98% (95% CI 95%–99%), specificity 84% (77%–89%), PPV 92% (90%–95%), NPV 94% (90%–97%) and accuracy 93% (91%–95%).

Added September 30, 2026 · DOI:10.1002/alz.71887; PMID:42805946; PMCID:PMC13619724

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

This is unusually useful post-implementation evidence because it joins clinical validity to longitudinal analytical surveillance rather than reporting a one-time research-cohort AUC. Definite results were accurate in a tertiary specialty population, but nearly one quarter were intermediate and renal impairment shifted more amyloid-negative patients into that category. Stable quality control and reagent comparisons support robustness of the local LDT; they do not validate every laboratory workflow or prove decision impact.

Study design

Investigators evaluated 744 unique Mayo Clinic patients with cognitive impairment seen from July 2024 through December 2025 at campuses in Minnesota, Florida and Arizona. Amyloid status was determined by florbetapir PET and/or CSF p-tau181/Aβ42 within one year of blood collection. Standalone plasma p-tau217 was measured on LUMIPULSE G1200 using pre-established negative, intermediate and positive cutpoints. Analytical monitoring spanned 18 months, 10 reagent lots, two reagent versions, twice-daily quality controls and a 187-sample version comparison.

Key quantitative results

  • Of 744 patients, 500 (67%) were amyloid-positive. Plasma p-tau217 results were positive in 421 (57%), intermediate in 169 (23%) and negative in 154 (21%). Excluding intermediate results, sensitivity was 98% (95% CI 95%–99%), specificity 84% (77%–89%), PPV 92% (90%–95%), NPV 94% (90%–97%) and accuracy 93% (91%–95%).
  • Against amyloid PET alone, sensitivity was 99% and specificity 69%; against CSF p-tau181/Aβ42, sensitivity was 95% and specificity 85%. PET and CSF themselves had 87% overall agreement among 76 patients tested with both methods.
  • Manufacturer-control imprecision was 5%–8%; an in-house pool near the negative cutpoint showed 12%–14% CV. Ten lot comparisons had R² above 0.990 and bias from ±2% to 11%; the reagent-version comparison (n=187) showed R² 0.99 and mean bias −4.35%. Reduced eGFR was associated with more intermediate results among amyloid-negative patients (adjusted p=0.008 for eGFR <45 versus at least 60 mL/min/1.73 m²).

What changed

A September 28 publication supplies 18-month, routine-practice evidence linking clinical classification performance with quality control, reagent-lot and assay-version surveillance for a standalone LUMIPULSE p-tau217 laboratory-developed test.

Strength of evidence

Strong implementation-oriented analytical robustness evidence from routine testing and pre-established cutpoints, with moderate clinical-validity evidence. Interpretation is limited by tertiary-specialty prevalence, two nonidentical reference standards, exclusion of intermediate results from accuracy estimates, few patients with severe renal impairment and a local LDT workflow that is not the FDA-cleared ratio product.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

The findings support sustained laboratory performance of this specific local workflow and reinforce the value of two-cutpoint interpretation and ongoing lot surveillance. A 23% intermediate rate and renal-function effects remain operationally important, and no patient-outcome or decision-impact benefit was tested.

Field medical relevance

Directly relevant to blood-biomarker implementation, cutpoint governance, quality assurance, renal-function interpretation and communication about the distinction between an LDT and an FDA-cleared assay.

Quanterix or platform relevance

The clinical workflow used a Mayo Clinic laboratory-developed standalone p-tau217 test with pre-established local cutpoints on the LUMIPULSE G1200. It is not the FDA-cleared Fujirebio pTau217/Aβ42 plasma ratio and should not inherit that product's labeled intended use.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No authorization, commercial-availability, guideline or coverage change occurred. The report concerns a Mayo Clinic LDT; laboratories adopting any workflow still need product- and matrix-specific validation, quality control and appropriate interpretation processes.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Was this the FDA-cleared LUMIPULSE plasma ratio?
No. The study used standalone LUMIPULSE p-tau217 with Mayo Clinic LDT cutpoints. The cleared Fujirebio product measures the pTau217/Aβ42 ratio under a different labeled intended use.
Does 93% accuracy include intermediate results?
No. Intermediate results, which occurred in 23% of patients, were excluded from sensitivity, specificity and accuracy calculations and require further evaluation.
Did the study establish clinical utility?
Not directly. It supports analytical robustness and clinical validity, but it did not test whether the workflow improves decisions, time to diagnosis, treatment access, safety, cost or patient outcomes.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Retrospective tertiary-center population with 67% amyloid prevalence
  • Mixed amyloid PET and CSF reference standards with only 87% agreement in paired cases
  • Intermediate results excluded from accuracy estimates despite comprising 23% of the cohort
  • Only 23 patients had eGFR below 45 mL/min/1.73 m²
  • Local LDT cutpoints and workflows may not transfer to other laboratories or products
  • No prospective decision-impact, health-economic, treatment-access or patient-outcome evaluation
